horizon_risk.caveat: Reduced to 200 Monte Carlo paths (vs. the retired 6-leg script's 2000) for runtime reasons -- disclosed, not hidden; see project_wheel_v1_horizon_risk.py's own module docstring. This is the FIRST run of this exact Monte Carlo methodology at the new no-permanent-derisk Policy B -- it has not been iterated/cross-checked across multiple runs the way the old script was over time. Read alongside, not instead of, the reconciled REAL backtest numbers: $4,015,457.63 final / 199.36% CAGR / -41.1% MDD over the real 4-year window, $14,013,277.60 / 155.87% CAGR / -54.6% MDD over the real 6-year window (Policy B, never derisks). The prior permanent-derisk policy's own real numbers ($939,296.63/108.19%/-28.2%/4yr T1=30%, $2,372,248.48/162.45%/-30.0%/4yr T1=70%; $1,479,308.37/75.89%/-27.3%/6yr T1=30%, $6,354,608.73/124.27%/-36.8%/6yr T1=70%) remain the retained comparison benchmarks. Policy B was adopted after an extensive margin-enforced Monte Carlo study (1,000 paths) found the graduated ramp alone reduces severe-loss frequency (>=70% of original capital) to an observed 0.1% without a permanent derisk switch -- an observed bootstrap frequency, not a calibrated forward probability. Note the much larger MDD figures here vs. the retained permanent-derisk benchmarks are the direct, expected cost of removing that switch -- not a new finding, the known tradeoff that was explicitly accepted when adopting Policy B.
horizon_risk.policy: Wheel v1.0, "Wheel Policy B" (active since 2026-10-27, adopted after an extensive margin-enforced leverage-survival study): T1=70%, D2 reversible leverage ladder (3x/4x/5x/6x, 15% hysteresis) -- the PERMANENT $500k->C30-B derisk switch has been REMOVED; the ladder holds at its own top rung (6x) indefinitely for any equity beyond 16x-of-start. Original permanent-derisk policy retained as a comparison benchmark, not deleted -- see wheel_v1_shadow_engine.py's LEGACY_* constants (LEGACY_DERISK_TRIGGER plus LEGACY_T1_WEIGHT/W_MNQ/W_MGC for the T1=30% point).
